title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials examining the effect of ultra-processed food on energy intake and weight gain
authors: Robinson E, Jones A, Evans R, Finlay A, Brealey J, Gough T, et al.
journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
population: 10 randomised trials comparing ultra-processed with less processed food
funder: Funding statement not read: the publisher's full text returned HTTP 403 to automated access, and the article is absent from PubMed Central and Europe PMC full text. Crossref metadata list no funder.
result: Pre-registered. Standardised mean differences for energy intake 0.18 to 0.44 in ultra-processed arms, with statistical significance varying between models; weight gain SMD 0.65 and eating rate SMD 0.96, both significant; palatability and appetite did not differ. Diets were not matched for nutrient profile. Energy intake SMD 0.71 when ultra-processed diets were more energy dense and 0.02 when energy density was similar. Certainty of evidence low. Results read from the PubMed abstract.
